instagram_caption:
He slid the report across the desk and said everyone signs it. The numbers in it were not true.

He has rent. His sister has fees. And the pen has been in his hand for an hour.

Jesus does not hand him a speech. He hands him a question: ask where the numbers came from. Men who are lying do not like being asked twice.

There is always a door out of the room. It is rarely the loud one. But God will not let you be pushed past what you can carry.

If you are standing over something you know you should not sign, ask the question first. 🤍
youtube_title: Jesus... They Want Me To Sign Something That Isn't True | Jesus Replies
youtube_description:
A young man is handed a report with numbers that are not true, and told that everyone signs it, nobody checks, and his name on it is only a formality.

He has rent to pay and his sister's fees to cover, and honesty suddenly feels like something he cannot afford.

Jesus does not give him a speech to deliver. He gives him a question to ask: where did these numbers come from? Because there is always a door out of the room, and it is rarely the loud one.

"No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to mankind. And God is faithful; he will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, he will also provide a way out so that you can endure it." - 1 Corinthians 10:13 (NIV)

If you have ever been asked to stay quiet about something wrong, this one is for you.
